summary.name: Line Art (Drawing and Illustration). The label was normalized from source descriptions, so the original name is not confirmed.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicitly, objects are described through contours, structural lines, and limited internal detail on a simple background. A consistent line-weight hierarchy is required, with small accent colors for emphasis. Line components can be revealed or moved while connected joints and controlled stroke widths are preserved.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly good fits: product and editorial introductions, explanatory and illustrated narratives, and abstract or cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. Elegant product or icon reveals are noted as working alone. Inferred: technical explanation or editorial layouts when paired with supporting styles.
summary.limitations: Explicitly, Animated Line Art should be avoided as a near-duplicate pairing. Chapter structures should be adapted or omitted when the topic is too short, or when transitions obscure causality. Rough.js sketch treatment applies only when the brief calls for it, not to precise grids, clean vectors, UI, or photorealistic assets. Hatching does not establish authentic pencil or print media.
summary.palette: These are suggested values, not supplied exact colors: background #FAF8F1 as the quiet field, foreground #273D42 for contours and text, and accent #B77843 as one small warm accent. Gradients are disabled. Foreground and background reach a 10.785 contrast ratio. The accent on background is 3.418, so it is decorative only. Task-supplied exact colors override these values.
summary.motionAndInteraction: The source specifies reveal or movement of line components while preserving joints and stroke widths, typically through stroke length or path segments. Optional motion references are motion-012 (chapter handoff) and motion-015 (scroll storytelling). Each should be used only if it fits the actual scene, and choosing neither is valid. Video is driven by seekable composition time. Interactive scroll is optional, and direct and backward seeks must be verified.
summary.audio: The style itself specifies no audio. The audio direction is a task-level suggestion only, with no mandatory genre, tempo, voice, or audio layer. Music, voiceover, sound effects, ambience, or silence may be proposed from the topic and objective. Explicit user audio choices and supplied assets take priority. Speech intelligibility, balance, clipping, and picture sync must be verified in the final video.
summary.assetRequirements: Contours should be stored as paths, with stroke caps, joins, and scaled line weights kept consistent. Fonts and imported assets must be loaded before rendering. Exact copy and existing assets are unspecified. Rough.js, Paper.js, and tldraw are optional preparation tools. Source artwork and approved palettes must be preserved, and SVG import fidelity, fonts, and raster content should be verified.
summary.combinations: Suggested pairing with style-097 suits mechanism explanation: outline, structure, and detail hierarchy, with #B77843 only on the active element and no filled shapes. Suggested pairing with style-019 suits editorial typography: #273D42 for both line and text, figures kept inside grid frames, and no colored section backgrounds. Both pairings are inferred suitability, not explicit source requirements.
summary.productionApproach: The style renderer owns drawing, using SVG paths with DrawSVGPlugin, and optionally Paper.js or Rough.js. The motion engine owns reveals, using GSAP DrawSVGPlugin or optionally Motion, with one owner per property. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline, and Remotion is used only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, with the reason recorded. Check keyframes, decoded video, palette, and audio sync.
